newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice ends mixed in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice ends mixed in dull trade.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended mixed on Friday and institutions continued to dominate market movements, traders said.

The key September 1996 contract ended limit-up at 2,496 ($300) per tonne, rising 36 yuan. It opened limit-up and stayed at that level for the whole session. October ended limit-down at 2,431 yuan per tonne, down 44 yuan.
Combined volume fell to 1,100 tonnes from 10,600.
Traders said institutions used their large capital to dominate the market despite poor fundamentals.
"Retail investors were forced to liquidate their short positions, which caused sharp rises," one trader said.
Traders said that rice moved sharply in a wide range during the past week, with heavy institutional trading squeezing out many individual stop-loss orders.
Analysts said that there would be an increase in stop-loss orders and no clear direction in the next few days.
